name: stakovr
description: bsh grows its string stack before writing, not on a write fault.  2.11BSD sh's macro.c pushes an expansion onto the stak with no bound and relies on the MEMF fault (fault.c:29) to grow the break when it runs past; FGX has no write fault, so the push runs past the break silently.  The script doubles $x by expansion to 16 KB, then expands it four times, which is more than the data bank holds: the shell must report `no space' and exit, and never reach the line after.  Without the guard the 64 KB push wraps the bank's 16-bit offset over the shell's own globals.  The markers are built from quoted halves so the typed command line cannot satisfy them.
